acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Goblins family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Raider, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Door-Shield Breacher (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Stands nearly upright in riveted plate scavenged from three different armies, carrying a real sword and a full door shield with exposed hinges, rope handles, and crude viewing slot.

Signature mechanic: Claimed Door: the Raider braces its scavenged door shield through incoming fire, then slams the lower edge into the ground to create one-way cover for smaller Goblins; planting commits the shield and leaves the sword arm and back exposed.
battlefieldDuty: Change the shape of the encounter by carrying mobile cover into a firing lane, then planting it as a temporary barricade that creates a Goblin advance route.
constructionDimensions: Materials and equipment become a stolen incendiary kit: oil-soaked rope, pitch-daubed door shields, heat-blued scrap, charred wood, ceramic fuel flasks, and fuse-bound cleavers remain visibly mismatched and field-repaired.
Silhouette and active effects expose fuel flow: high-mounted flask racks, trailing fuse cords, directional smoke, and pulsing shield-vent embers make ignition routes readable before flames spread.
counterplay: Interrupt before the rope locks, flank the exposed sword side after planting, cut the visible brace to topple the door, or force the Raider away so the claimed lane no longer advances with it. Affinity signal: A fuse spits bright sparks from flask to weapon or lootworks station before ignition; cutting that cord or breaking the clearly mounted fuel flask cancels the empowered action.
forbiddenTreatments: Uniform orange recolor without fuel-bearing construction changes
Glow-only fire treatment without visible fuel, combustion hardware, or heat response
Fire made from the Goblin's flesh rather than scavenged fuel and equipment
Clean forged flame armor that no longer reads as stolen scrap
identityInvariants: Short, hunched, long-armed humanoid silhouette with an oversized head and pointed ears, disproportionately large hands and feet, hooked nose, and crowded crooked teeth.
Sickly green or gray-green skin against muddy browns, rust-orange, dull iron, and sparse accents of stolen gold.
Every carried object reads as stolen, scavenged, or crudely repaired: rags, patched leather, cracked wood, rusted scrap metal, bone, and rope rather than purpose-built matching equipment.
Loot is the status language: mismatched helmets, coin necklaces, teeth, rings, captured banners, and trophies accumulate with rank.
Posture and finish communicate hierarchy, from a knock-kneed cringing crouch to an upright swagger amid increasingly prestigious plunder.
telegraph: It turns the door broadside, peers through a hacked eye slot, and drags a bright rope brace taut before the ground-slam.
